summary: Harper was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Muskingum University and under William Dwight Whitney at Yale University (Dr. phil. 1875). He was a professor at Yale and president of the University of Chicago (1891–1906).

William Reeve worked in linguistics and Indology. He served as a missionary with the London Missionary Society (c. 1816–1824 and c. 1827–1834) and later as a minister at Oswestry Congregational Church (1836–1843).
A historian, William Robertson studied divinity at the University of Edinburgh from 1733 to 1741. He later served as the university's principal from 1762 to 1792.

Hardie studied at the University of Edinburgh (c. 1876–1880) and Balliol College, Oxford (c. 1880–1884). He later held academic posts at the University of Oxford (c. 1884–1895) and the University of Edinburgh (c. 1895–1916).

Active in Indology, Roxburgh studied medicine at Edinburgh under John Hope and Alexander Monro, and at Marischal College. He served as Chief Botanist for the East India Company and superintendent of the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden (1793–1813).

Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Waldron completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota, Ichijo Ogawa, and Seiki Miyashita. He held posts as a researcher at Otani University and faculty at Middlebury College (attested 2003).

A scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology, Vaux studied at Balliol College, Oxford (BA c. 1840, MA c. 1842). He was Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (1861–1870) and Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1876–1885).
Active in Indology and religious studies, William Sax held an academic post at the University of Canterbury (attested 2000) and served as Professor Emeritus at Heidelberg University in 2025.

A scholar in linguistics and Indology, Allen earned his PhD at Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey and Arthur James Beattie. He lectured in phonetics at SOAS (1948–1951) and was Professor of Comparative Philology at Cambridge (1955–1982).
Spottiswoode, active in Indology, attended Eton College and Harrow School before studying at Balliol College, Oxford (1842–1845). In 1846, he held posts at Balliol College and at Eyre & Spottiswoode.

Stede was an Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Leipzig (c. 1910–1913). He taught Pāli at SOAS (1926–1949) and served as President of the Pali Text Society (1950–1958).
William Taylor worked in the field of Indology. He served as a missionary with the London Missionary Society from 1824 to 1845 and worked as a cataloguer at Madras College.

A scholar in Buddhist and religious studies, Van Gordon founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research and held a post as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University (attested 2015).

Active in Indology and religious studies, Ward studied at Ewood Hall Academy under John Fawcett and at Brearley Theological Academy. He served as a missionary at Serampore Mission (c. 1799–1823) and co-founded Serampore College in 1818.

Active in Indology, history, and archaeology, Webb studied at the University of Aberdeen. He served in the Indian Medical Service and the Bengal Army, and later was secretary at the Army Medical School (1893–1902).

Hunter was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Glasgow, Paris, and Bonn, he served in the Indian Civil Service (c. 1862–1887) and was Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1886–1887).

Rockhill worked in Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École spéciale militaire de Saint-Cyr (c. 1871–1873) and pursued scholarly training in France under Léon Feer and Philippe Édouard Foucaux (c. 1875–1880).

A scholar of linguistics, Wright studied at St Andrews, Halle-Wittenberg, and Leiden. He served as Professor of Arabic at Trinity College Dublin (1856–1861), Assistant Keeper at the British Museum (1861–1870), and Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge (1870–1889).
Yates was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bristol Baptist College and Brown University. He also studied under William Carey from approximately 1815 to 1834.
An Indologist, Kirfel earned his PhD (1908) under Hermann Jacobi and completed his Habilitation at the University of Bonn. He subsequently served as professor of Indology at Bonn from 1922 to 1953.
